notes: Found by job-scout; Cologne; apply via jobs.rewe-group.com; gaps Snowflake/BigQuery/Databricks, Terraform, GCP; German likely used day to day (B1)
apply_hint: Apply via the REWE Group careers site (jobs.rewe-group.com); the LinkedIn posting is https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4386355137. The posting asks for availability and salary expectation in the online application.
verdict: Strong on the GenAI/MLOps side (hands-on GenAI projects, Python, CI/CD, Docker/Kubernetes, Azure, IaC with AWS CDK) and on solution architecture. Real gaps on the platform-tooling side: no hands-on Snowflake/BigQuery/Databricks, no Terraform, no GCP, and "mehrjährige" platform/DevOps experience is only partly covered (3 years, AI engineering with DevOps parts).

form_fields.label: Why REWE digital?
form_fields.value: You already run GenAI for 20,000 administrative staff and process over a billion records a day; a self-service platform for analytics, ML and GenAI makes every team faster, and that is the work I want to do.

form_fields.label: Salary expectation
form_fields.value: €70,000 gross/year (range €60,000–75,000). Must be above the EU Blue Card threshold.

form_fields.label: Location
form_fields.value: Cologne; hybrid works well, willing to relocate.

questions.q: How would you build a self-service GenAI platform for many business teams?
questions.a: Shared gateway for LLM access (one API, per-team budgets and allowed models, logging of cost/latency), onboarding by config in a PR, templates and best-practice docs, central evaluation and monitoring. Evidence: LiteLLM as the LLM layer at Kniit; MCP service that other tools use; if built, demo the LLM Gateway.

questions.q: Tell us about your infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD experience.
questions.a: AWS CDK at Covestro (agentic app on AWS; Lambda/SQS/DynamoDB for thesis evaluation); GitLab CI/CD; Docker; Kubernetes and Azure at Kniit. Be honest: no Terraform in a job; same concepts (state, plan/apply, modules).
Honest: not in a job yet. SQL, Postgres, MongoDB, Neo4j, DynamoDB in practice; BigQuery in the LLM Gateway project once built.
